t.PROPYLPARABEN.agn: In the EU its sum with butylparaben may be at most 0.14% (as acid); it may not be used in leave-on products for the nappy area of children under 3 (Annex V, entry 12a). It is on the EU priority list of potential endocrine disruptors (group A); in 2021 the SCCS found it safe at the 0.14% limit. Denmark banned it in products for children under 3.
t.PROPYLPARABEN.eff.0: Put on the EU priority list over a suspected effect on the hormone system; the SCCS found it safe at the 0.14% limit.
t.PROPYLPARABEN.k3.0: EU priority list of potential endocrine disruptors (group A). SCCS 2021: safe at a maximum of 0.14%; banned in products applied to the nappy area of children under 3 years of age.
t.PROPYLPARABEN.k3.1: Denmark. Denmark banned this substance nationally, ahead of the EU, in cosmetics intended for children under 3 years of age because of suspected endocrine disruption.
t.PROPYLPARABEN.pw.0: In the EU it may not be used in leave-on products for the nappy area of children under 3.
t.PROPYLPARABEN.reg.0: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex V, entry 12: Permitted preservative, with an upper limit.
t.PROPYLPARABEN.reg.1: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex V, entry 12a: Permitted preservative, with an upper limit.
t.PROPYLPARABEN.summary: A preservative from the paraben group.
t.PROPYLPARABEN.what: Prevents the product from spoiling through bacteria and fungi.
